// L I.4 SB "I" 27

lines.translation: #tr.en: Pick up the tablet of lapis lazuli and read out,

%n umma | libittaša | lā agurrat
// L I.4 SB "I" 20

lines.translation: #tr.en: thus: “Is not its brickwork kiln-fired brick,

%n uššīšu | lā iddû || sebet | muntalkū

lines.translation: #tr.en: did the seven sages not lay its foundations?

%n šār (|) ālu | šār (|) kirâtu | šār (|) essû | pitir (|) bīt (|) ištar
// L I.4 SB "I" 22

lines.translation: #tr.en: One @i{šār} is city, one @i{šār} date-grove, one @i{šār} is clay pit, half a @i{šār} the temple of Ištar:

%n šalāšat (|) šār | u pitir || uruk | ...
// L I.4 SB "I" 23

manuscripts.atf: ša-la-aš₂! ša-ri u₃ pi-tir u₂-ru-uk x x x

lines.translation: #tr.en: three @i{šār} and a half (is) Uruk, (@i{its}) @i{measurement}.”

ul-ta-dir GURUŠ!-MEŠ ša UNUG!{ki} ina ku-x x

lines.translation: #tr.en: he had hair (that was dark) like lapis-coloured wool.

lines.translation: #tr.en: a triple cubit @i{the whiskers} of his cheeks.
